idiom_name: Akka/Pekko ask: ref ? Message returning Future[Reply]
implementation_notes: Akka's ask pattern is the library form of request-reply: `ref ? msg` (classic, from akka.pattern.ask) or `ref.ask(...)` (typed) attaches a temporary response actor as the reply channel and returns a Future that completes with the reply or fails with AskTimeoutException when the implicit Timeout expires - the correlation is the temporary actor, so no message identifier is needed. Without an actor system, scala.concurrent.Promise/Future plus a correlation map is the manual fallback, and deadline propagation across hops stays the application's job. Akka changed licence in 2022; Apache Pekko is the open-source fork with the same API.
code_sketch:
import akka.pattern.ask
import akka.util.Timeout
import scala.concurrent.duration.*
implicit val timeout: Timeout = 5.seconds
val quote: Future[Quote] = (pricing ? GetQuote(symbol)).mapTo[Quote]
quote.recover { case _: AskTimeoutException => Quote.unavailable(symbol) }
pitfalls: ask creates a temporary actor per request, so high-rate use means actor churn and a mailbox per call; typed request-response protocols or streams are better for hot paths.
The timeout expires the Future, not the work: the target may still finish and reply to a dead actor (dead letters), so treat it as a client-side decision only.
Never Await.result inside a receiving actor: it blocks a dispatcher thread and can deadlock the system; compose with map/flatMap or pipeTo.
